body_markdown:
Feelings aren’t necessarily grounded in facts, but they do a great job motivating us to take action. Or at least it “feels” that way sometimes, and I am going through such a moment as we speak. Because while the mind understands the value in air travel, my heart is very interested in a days-long interstate drive to accomplish what happens in a matter of hours on a plane.


My last few experiences at the airport have been perfectly acceptable, but I must admit that all the news surrounding airport delays, parked planes on runways, and just a general feeling of discontent from travelers has soured my relationship with air travel. At least that’s the case for traveling in these United States, though a similar problem recently flared up[in the U.K.](https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/airports-uk-report-disruptions-after-technical-issue-national-136275963) , much to my dismay. So when I planned a future (October) trip to the famous Laguna Seca Raceway, I jumped at the chance to make it a road trip with a friend instead.


After accepting that friend’s generous offer, I pondered how “spoiled” I’ve become with air travel. My mother has a travel agency that was once laden with travel perks. I’ve had several corporate jobs that let me jet-set across the U.S. and the U.K., but my days of preferred statuses with air/hotel/rental car organizations are in my rearview. So I fondly remember when my mother didn’t have a travel agency, and she was a stay-at-home mom. We would take interstate road trips at least once a year, many occurring when my father owned a 1975 Mercury Montego MX.


Sajeev Mehta (Actually his Dad)


Sajeev Mehta (Actually his Dad)


I was just a toddler (see trunk photo above), but I vaguely remember extended periods in the Montego’s cavernous rear bench seat as we drove to Florida and California from our home in Houston. I am looking forward to rekindling some of this magic next month when I drive to Monterey, California.


I am pretty sure the longest road trip of my life was going to Disney World in that yellow Mercury Montego, but I know that length is far from worthy of a trophy. And that’s where I hand it off to you, dear reader, as I ask:


**What was your longest Road Trip?**
